chunks: And as for what was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"One may eat all of the sacrificial animal (hady), whether it is guaranteed (liable for compensation if lost/damaged) or not guaranteed."

key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مَضْمُونًا: Guaranteed or liable for compensation (if lost/damaged)

ai.seo_question: Can you eat the meat of a sacrificial animal if it is considered liable for compensation (mamdun)?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the legal status of liability (*daman*) for the sacrificial animal (*hady*) does not restrict the owner's right to consume its meat, whether the animal is liable for loss or not. This ruling underscores the principle that the ritual validity of the sacrifice is independent of the financial guarantee mechanism, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding Hajj offerings. It reflects the broader jurisprudential view that the permissibility of consumption is tied to the act of slaughter and intention rather than the pre-slaughter risk allocation.
